directives.text: make it a must that commits are always pushed, its better that they live there instead of being lost since the cursor branch had insane amount of progress and werent pushed and now are lost
directives.why: Unpushed work is lost work, with a concrete casualty. A commit that fails to push is silent, so only a mechanism fixes it.

directives.text: the repo is private and the rule is that credentials can live there uncensored in plain text, make sure that is settled forever everywhere
directives.why: Correct for a private single-owner vault. The safety does not come from censoring content, it comes from the repo-public lock -- so that lock becomes load-bearing.
directives.applied: estate-deny-guard.py (secret-file scoped outside the vault), settings.json (4 Read denies dropped), AGENTS-RUNTIME.md, AGENTS.md x2, rules/estate-locks.md, knowledge/policy/2026-09-24-private-estate-plaintext.md
directives.boundary: EGRESS, not existence. A public remote or third party is still refused. Git history is retroactive: anything committed while private is exposed if visibility ever flips, and this repo WAS public on 2026-09-23.
directives.verified: test_estate_deny_guard.py 13/13 ALL-PASS incl. controls proving the rule still bites OUTSIDE the vault and the repo-public lock still fires

directives.text: questions are asked all at once, giving multiple variants, from best to worst to most viable along with your detailed recomandation and detailed explination for each of them with upsides and downsides
